features.title: Quay walls along the Douro
features.user_visible_behavior: The river edge in Ribeira and Gaia has built quay walls, not a bare terrain edge.
verification: Visual: Cais da Ribeira and Cais de Gaia show stone walls at water level
evidence: scripts/fetch-quays.mjs writes data/quays.json (20 lines, 7.4 km) from OSM river-polygon edges on the Ribeira, Gaia and Foz reaches and next to retaining walls; OSM has no man_made=quay in the core
src/quays.js: granite wall (5 courses, tide-line course), coping, deck, skirt, hexagonal bollards every 30 m (248), merged per 1 km cell (15 meshes, 34 k triangles); heights from heightAt
Screenshots read: Ribeira and Gaia with and without the layer; Commons references read (Ribeira quay, Cais de Gaia)
Session 005: the wall moves river-ward (up to 22 m, smoothed) to where heightAt meets the water, so the DEM pad leaves no green terrain wedge in front of it (commit 45d8443)
features.notes: NOT done: the terrain behind the wall is not flattened. The ground mesh is 27 m per cell and the water drapes on heightAt, so a flat pad would lift the water. The wall stands on the water line with a 3-12 m deck that reaches inland until the ground meets it. Foz not checked closely. The arcaded Ribeira front is out of scope.

features.title: Geometry LOD for buildings and tiles
features.user_visible_behavior: Far buildings and tiles draw fewer triangles, so weak devices hold the frame rate.
verification: Measure frame time before and after on a low-tier profile
evidence: Triangles (renderer.info), desktop 1440x900: first frames 4.69 M -> 1.97 M peak; settled overview 3.04 M -> 1.76 M; mid 3.98 M -> 3.41 M; close 3.94 M -> 3.37 M. Mobile 390x844: first frame 2.26 M -> 1.25 M, settled 1.11 M

src/scene.js ground index LOD (every 2nd/4th grid line far away); src/roads.js setGeoLod (street lines body quads only, minor lines and, on phones, minor ribbons dropped); src/main.js applyGeoLod and the 700-unit shadow cap from the first frame; core building tiers now update from frame 1
Screenshot pairs read: overview and Luis I before and after
features.notes: Landmark far LOD, the building tiers and tile near/far LOD already existed. Not done: people/tree counts by tier, and the governor level only shifts the far thresholds (close-range triangles do not change with the governor). Mobile first frame is 4 % above the 1.2 M target.

features.title: Device classes, capability detection, governor v2, quality menu, perf overlay
features.user_visible_behavior: The app picks Ultra, High, Medium, Low or Potato from the GPU name, memory, cores, screen and display cadence; a menu entry (Image > Quality) and ?quality= override it; ?perf=1 or Shift+P shows fps, p95, class, pressure, GPU and JS memory and exports a JSON of the session. A closed loop on p95 frame time cuts resolution first, then shadows, effects, counts and close-range geometry, and gives them back when there is headroom.
verification: node scripts/smoke-perf.mjs (class table, ladder, governor on a synthetic load schedule; part of npm run verify)
node scripts/perf-stress.mjs (class switching, context loss, freeze, ?quality=, reduced motion, offline, 300 s soak)
evidence: perf/BASELINE.md before/after table for five device profiles; laptop-igpu dropped frames 12.6 % -> 0, phone-low 54 % -> 0.3 %
soak 300 s: JS heap 190-195 MB (1.6 %), GL memory 628-667 MB (3 %), no console errors
WEBGL_lose_context: loss seen, restore, map redraws (screenshot read)
features.notes: Class table values for real GPUs are educated, not measured on those chips: perf/DEVICE-CHECKLIST.md lists what to test. Potato (software GL) is not usable: 2-4 s per frame.
